newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: No suit, no ceremony, Argentine cowboy is told.
newsitem.headline: No suit, no ceremony, Argentine cowboy is told.

text.p: An Argentine "gaucho" cowboy was told he could not attend his university graduation ceremony unless he swapped his traditional baggy trousers, medallioned belt and neckerchief for a suit and tie.

Walter Scibilia, a 26-year-old farm boy from Mendoza on the western edge of the broad pampa grasslands, was instead handed his diploma in agronomy inside the dean's office, La Nacion newspaper reported on Thursday.
Scibilia, furious and defiantly resplendent in his gaucho gear, said he always dressed that way back home on the family cattle ranch.

"I was born and bred on the land. That's where I work, it's the way I live with my family," he said. "What I wear is the best clothing for a country man, just like a suit and tie is for a yuppie working in the big city."
Dean Rosa Ines Arreghini of the University of Cuyo said she had had a long chat with Scibilia but that even gauchos had to dress like city slickers to graduate.
